mail.headDescription: The outgoing mail server. What the app may send through it lives under Notifications.
mail.intro: Point this at your mail provider or relay (e.g. a Gmail app password, Fastmail, or your own SMTP server). Most providers need an app password rather than your account password. The password is stored on the server and never shown again.
mail.implicitTls: Use implicit TLS (port 465). Leave off for STARTTLS on 587.
mail.testSentBody: A test email was sent to your account address. Check your inbox.
mail.testNote: The test uses the last saved settings, so save before testing.

missingPhotos.headDescription: Photos whose files have vanished from disk. They're hidden from the gallery but kept here — with their metadata and last-known thumbnail — in case the file comes back. Unmatched after the grace window, they're permanently removed by the weekly cleanup. If a drive was just offline, rescan the library and they revive.
missingPhotos.retentionInvalid: Enter a number of days (0 to keep missing photos forever).
missingPhotos.saveRetentionFailed: Unable to save the retention window
missingPhotos.empty: No missing photos — every catalogued photo is present on disk.
missingPhotos.confirmRemoveBody: Its catalog entry, cached thumbnail, and any detected faces are deleted. The file is already gone from disk, so there is nothing to restore — this only cleans up the leftover record. It cannot be undone.
missingPhotos.confirmPurgeAllBody_one: Every photo missing longer than {{count}} day has its catalog entry, thumbnail, and detected faces permanently removed. The files are already gone from disk. This cannot be undone.
missingPhotos.confirmPurgeAllBody_other: Every photo missing longer than {{count}} days has its catalog entry, thumbnail, and detected faces permanently removed. The files are already gone from disk. This cannot be undone.

storySettings.headDescription: Where story narration recordings are kept.
storySettings.intro: Recordings made in the story editor are saved into one gallery library you choose here, under “Story recordings”. They become ordinary audio in that library — visible in the gallery, included in backups, and kept even if their story is deleted. Until a library is chosen, the story editor offers no recording at all.
storySettings.libraryNote: Pick a library every member can view, or narration will be missing for people without access to it. Choosing a library also adds audio file types to its scan settings.
storySettings.pendingBody_one: {{count}} narration recording is stored inside the app, invisible to the gallery. Move it into the recordings library so it is backed up and browsable like everything else.
storySettings.pendingBody_other: {{count}} narration recordings are stored inside the app, invisible to the gallery. Move them into the recordings library so they are backed up and browsable like everything else.
storySettings.moveConfirmBody_one: {{count}} recording is copied into the recordings library and its story updated to play it from there. Stories keep working throughout; nothing is deleted until the copy has succeeded.
storySettings.moveConfirmBody_other: {{count}} recordings are copied into the recordings library and their stories updated to play them from there. Stories keep working throughout; nothing is deleted until each copy has succeeded.
storySettings.moveDoneBody_one: {{count}} recording now lives in the recordings library.
storySettings.moveDoneBody_other: {{count}} recordings now live in the recordings library.
storySettings.moveFailedBody_one: {{count}} recording could not be moved and was left in place — run this again after checking the library folder is writable.
storySettings.moveFailedBody_other: {{count}} recordings could not be moved and were left in place — run this again after checking the library folder is writable.

notifications.headDescription: What the app may email people about, beyond the mail they asked for.
notifications.intro: These are switched off until you turn them on. Security alerts, sign-in codes and “Send to e-reader” are unaffected either way — those are either asked for or too important to be optional.
notifications.noMailBody: Notifications need somewhere to send from. Set up an outgoing mail server under <lnk>Settings → Email</lnk>, then come back here.
notifications.shareDesc: Email someone when a photo, book, or album is shared with them. The message says who shared what and links to “Shared with me”; it never carries the file itself.
notifications.recommendDesc: Email someone when a family member sends them a book, photo or person. They see it in the app either way — this is only for households that would rather not have to look.

opds.headDescription: Open your ebooks in KOReader, Moon+ Reader or Thorium over OPDS.
opds.intro: Create a token for a device, then paste its catalog link into the reader. Each token is read-only and can be removed at any time.
opds.copyNowBody: This is the only time the token is shown. Paste the catalog link into your reader to finish.
opds.qrHint: Scan to add the catalog on a phone or tablet.
opds.deviceNameIntro: Name the device this token is for, so you can recognise it later.
opds.confirmRemoveBody: That device will lose access to your ebooks at its next catalog refresh. Your other devices are not affected.

recycleBin.loadFailed: Unable to load the Recycle Bin
recycleBin.refreshFailed: Unable to refresh the Recycle Bin
recycleBin.libraryFilterLabel: Which library's deleted items to show
recycleBin.blurbKeepDays_one: Deleted items keep their files here for {{count}} day
recycleBin.blurbKeepDays_other: Deleted items keep their files here for {{count}} days
recycleBin.blurbKeepForever: Deleted items keep their files here until you remove them
recycleBin.blurbCleanupForever: , and duplicate cleanup removals stay until you remove them
recycleBin.blurbSuffix: Every item shows its own date — changing these settings never moves a date already given.
recycleBin.searchLabel: Search deleted items by name, folder or library
recycleBin.binsKeptMulti: Deleted files are kept in each library's own folder:
recycleBin.emptyLocationPath: Deleted files will go to <cd>{{path}}</cd> — change this under the <btn>bin's settings</btn>.
recycleBin.emptyLocationDefault: Deleted files will go to a hidden <cd>.trash</cd> folder inside each library — change this under the <btn>bin's settings</btn>.
recycleBin.noticeTitle: Some items stayed in the bin
recycleBin.viewOptionsTitle: View options — per page, order and how long items are kept
recycleBin.emptyTitleScoped: Empty the Recycle Bin for {{name}} — other libraries are left alone
recycleBin.emptyTitleAll: Empty the whole Recycle Bin — every library
recycleBin.noMatchRetention: Nothing in the bin is kept for that long.
recycleBin.noMatchSourceLibrary: Nothing removed that way from that library.
recycleBin.duplicateBadgeTitle: A duplicate copy, removed by a duplicate cleanup
recycleBin.keptForLabel: How long the item is kept for
recycleBin.daysUntilEmpty: days (0 = until you empty the bin)
recycleBin.retentionNote: Every item keeps the date it was given when it was deleted, so changing these never moves a date already set. They decide what happens from now on.
recycleBin.locationLockedTitle: Empty the Recycle Bin first — the location can only change while it holds nothing
recycleBin.daysInvalid: Days must be a whole number, 0 or more.
recycleBin.cleanupDaysInvalid: Days must be a whole number, 0 or more — or blank to follow the Recycle Bin.
recycleBin.saveRetentionFailed: Unable to save the retention settings
recycleBin.emptyFailed: Unable to empty the Recycle Bin
recycleBin.noPermission_one: {{count}} you don't have permission to restore
recycleBin.noPermission_other: {{count}} you don't have permission to restore
recycleBin.purgeBody_one: Its {{count}} file will be erased from disk. This cannot be undone — restore it instead if you might want it back.
recycleBin.purgeBody_other: Its {{count}} files will be erased from disk. This cannot be undone — restore it instead if you might want it back.
recycleBin.restoreAllBodyScoped: Everything the bin holds for <bold>{{name}}</bold> goes back where it came from — its files return to their library folder and it appears in the library again. Deleted items in other libraries are left alone.
recycleBin.restoreAllBodyAll: Everything in the bin goes back where it came from — files return to their library folders and the items appear in their libraries again.
recycleBin.restoreAllBodyShared: Each is put back on its own, so one that can't be — its library has been removed, or something else now occupies the place it came from — doesn't stop the rest. Anything that can't go back stays in the bin and is named here afterwards. Nothing is deleted either way.
recycleBin.emptyDialogStats: <bold>{{items}}</bold> · {{size}} · {{files}} will be permanently deleted, including their files on disk. This cannot be undone.
recycleBin.unexpiredAll: Every one of them is still inside its retention window — none was due to go yet.
recycleBin.unexpiredSome_one: <bold>{{count}}</bold> of them is still inside the retention window it was given, and would not have gone on its own.
recycleBin.unexpiredSome_other: <bold>{{count}}</bold> of them are still inside the retention window they were given, and would not have gone on their own.
recycleBin.emptyScopeOnly: Only <bold>{{name}}</bold> is emptied. Deleted items in other libraries are left alone.
recycleBin.emptyReachesAll: This reaches every library, including any the page is not currently showing. To empty just one, choose it in the library filter first.

scanRules.intro: Custom rules scan specific folders with their own layout, overriding the default scan there. Changes take effect on the next rescan.
scanRules.ebookOnlyBody: Scan rules currently apply when scanning ebook libraries.
scanRules.emptyList: No scan rules yet. Add one to organize an unusual folder.
scanRules.noFoldersChosen: No folders chosen yet — browse the library to add one or more.
scanRules.patternHelp: Folders are separated by “/”; text between tokens is matched literally. Use {ignore} for a folder level you don't want to map.
scanRules.previewHint: Choose folders and a pattern to preview.
scanRules.noMatches: No files matched in those folders.
scanRules.footerHint: Add a name, at least one folder, and a pattern to save.
scanRules.pickerIntro: Browsing <bold>{{name}}</bold>. Open a folder to go deeper, then add the ones this rule should scan.
scanRules.deleteBody: The rule's folders return to the default scanner on the next rescan. No catalog data is removed now.

scheduledJobs.intro: Recurring upkeep tasks. Pick how often each one runs — and on which day, at what time — or turn it off entirely. Changes save as you make them. <bold>Run now</bold> starts one immediately.

protection.proxyNoteAttention: Requests carry X-Forwarded-For but neither TRUST_PROXY nor TRUST_PROXY_HOPS is set — every visitor may look like the proxy
protection.proxyNoteAddresses: A reverse proxy fronts the app; forwarding headers are believed only from its own addresses
protection.proxyNoteHops: A reverse proxy fronts the app and the client address is read past it
protection.proxyNoteDirect: No reverse proxy in front — fine at home, a thin front door on the internet
protection.mfaNoteFallback: Email fallback for anyone not enrolled
protection.mfaNoteNoMail: Email is not set up — the un-enrolled have no fallback
protection.alertsNoteOn: Emailed when an account signs in from a new network
protection.alertsNoteNoMail: On, but email is not set up
protection.alertsNoteOff: A sign-in from a new network is not announced
protection.deletesNoteOn: Deletes are refused from outside the house
protection.deletesNoteNoNetworks: On, but no trusted network is defined — deletes are refused everywhere
protection.deletesNoteOff: Anyone signed in can delete from any network
protection.devicesNoteLocal: A TV can only be linked from inside the house
protection.devicesNoteAny: Linking can be started from the internet
protection.pwNoteComplex: At least three of: lowercase, uppercase, numbers, symbols
protection.pwNoteLength: Length only — any characters will do
protection.repNoteAddKey: Add a key to score blocked addresses
protection.strongDetail: Your settings block the common threats and layer several protections.
protection.goodDetail: A setting or two could be tighter — the amber and red rows below say which.
protection.fairDetail: Several protections are off or weak for the way this server is reached.
protection.weakDetail: Most of the protections that matter here are off. Start with the red rows.
protection.criticalDetail: Almost nothing stands between a stranger and the sign-in screen.
protection.heading: Protection level
protection.tooltipInternet: Graded for a server reachable from the internet: every protection counts, and proxy trust, a second factor from outside and sign-in alerts count most — they are how you keep strangers out and hear about the ones who got close.
protection.tooltipInternal: Graded for a server on the home network only: the same exam, but the defences that only matter against strangers — proxy trust, a second factor from outside, deletion protection, IP reputation — are waived and credited in full, and sign-in alerts and device linking count half. The same settings never score lower at home than on the internet.
protection.hintProxyTrusted: A proxy is in front of this server — if it can be reached from the internet, switch the grading above.
protection.hintProxyUntrusted: Requests are arriving through a proxy the app does not trust. If this server can be reached from the internet, say so above — the grading is gentler than it should be until then.

security.descOverview: How sign-in protection is currently set up.
security.descPolicies: Lockout, IP auto-blocking, password rules and sign-in alerts.
security.descTrusted: Networks that skip the IP auto-block, such as your own LAN.
security.descBlocked: Addresses that cannot reach the sign-in screen.
security.policiesSubtitle: Each row opens the setting that owns it
security.thresholdsDesc: Tune the lockout and IP auto-block. Changes apply immediately.
security.lockAfterHelp: Number of consecutive failed sign-in attempts.
security.autoblockAfterHelp: Number of failed sign-ins before an IP is blocked.
security.failWindowHelp: Time window to count failed sign-ins from the same IP.
security.mfaDesc: Whether a password alone is enough to sign in from outside your trusted networks.
security.mfaLabel: Require a second factor outside trusted networks
security.mfaHelp: Even a stolen or guessed password is then not enough to get in from the internet. Accounts with two-factor set up use their usual method; accounts without get a one-time code emailed to their sign-in address. Passkey sign-ins already count as two factors. At home — on a trusted network — nothing changes.
security.mfaNoMailBody: The emailed-code fallback needs SMTP, configured under Control panel → Settings → Email. Without it, accounts that haven't set up two-factor cannot sign in from outside at all until they enroll from home.
security.usersWithoutMail_one: {{list}} — this account will get a code by email when signing in from outside.
security.usersWithoutMail_other: {{list}} — these accounts will get a code by email when signing in from outside.
security.usersWithoutNoMail_one: {{list}} — this account will be unable to sign in from outside until two-factor is set up or email is configured.
security.usersWithoutNoMail_other: {{list}} — these accounts will be unable to sign in from outside until two-factor is set up or email is configured.
security.proxyAsksTitle: Every sign-in will ask for the second factor
security.proxyAsksBody: Requests arrive through a proxy but neither <cd>TRUST_PROXY</cd> nor <cd>TRUST_PROXY_HOPS</cd> is set, so the server cannot tell who is on a trusted network. With this policy on, it plays safe and asks everyone — including at home — until you set one.
security.alertsDesc: Warn about a successful sign-in from somewhere the account has never been used.
security.alertsLabel: Email on a sign-in from a new network
security.alertsHelp: The account owner and the admins are emailed. Networks are matched loosely (the /24 for IPv4, the /64 for IPv6) so a changing home or mobile address doesn't alert every time. Sign-ins from trusted networks never alert.
security.alertsNoMailBody: These alerts are sent over SMTP. Configure it under Control panel → Settings → Email, or this setting has no effect.
security.ipsInaccurateBody: Requests arrive through a proxy but neither <cd>TRUST_PROXY</cd> nor <cd>TRUST_PROXY_HOPS</cd> is set, so every visitor looks like the proxy address. Until you set one, a new network is never detected.
security.deletesDesc: Keep destructive actions to networks you trust, so stolen credentials used from the internet can't destroy the library.
security.deletesLabel: Allow deletions only from trusted networks
security.deletesHelp: Applies to every account, admins included. Away from home, everything still works — browsing, uploads, edits, progress — but deleting items, emptying the Recycle Bin, cleaning up duplicates, and restoring backups are refused until you're back on a trusted network.
security.noTrustedBody: With this on and no trusted networks, nobody can delete anything from anywhere. Add your home network under Trusted networks, or turn this off.
security.devicesDesc: Where a TV, display or kiosk may ask to be signed in from by showing a code.
security.devicesLocalLabel: Only devices on your home network
security.devicesLocalHelp: The recommended setting. A wall display is always in the house, and this is what stops a stranger elsewhere from starting a request at all.
security.devicesAnyLabel: Any device that can reach the server
security.devicesAnyHelp: Needed only if you link devices while away from home. It also lets someone else start a request and send you its code — approving one still needs your password, so never approve a device you didn't just set up, and check the code matches the screen in front of you.
security.linkRefusedBody: Requests arrive through a proxy but neither <cd>TRUST_PROXY</cd> nor <cd>TRUST_PROXY_HOPS</cd> is set, so every device looks like it is on the proxy's own address — which would make "home network only" mean "anyone at all". Linking is refused entirely until you set one.
security.pwDesc: Applies when a password is set or changed. Existing passwords keep working.
security.pwMixLabel: Require a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols (at least 3 of 4)
security.pwMixHelp: Improve password strength by requiring character variety.
security.repDesc: Look up addresses this server has already flagged against AbuseIPDB's community database, and show the result next to each blocked IP.
security.repKeyHelp: Free at abuseipdb.com. Leave empty to keep reputation lookups off — with a key set, addresses that trip the auto-block (and ones you check by hand) are sent to AbuseIPDB. Only already-flagged addresses are ever looked up, never regular visitors.
security.repKeySavedNote: A key is saved; type a new one to replace it.
security.repEscalateLabel: Make auto-blocks permanent for known abusive IPs
security.repEscalateHelp: When an address gets auto-blocked and AbuseIPDB reports it above the score below, the block keeps no expiry instead of the usual cooldown. You can always unblock it by hand.
security.repThresholdLabel: Abuse confidence score to escalate at (50–100)
security.repThresholdHelp: AbuseIPDB's 0–100 confidence that an address is abusive. 90+ keeps false positives rare.
security.exposureFailed: Unable to save how the server is reached
security.trustedDesc: Requests from these ranges skip rate limits, account lockout, and two-factor — handy on your home LAN. Leave empty unless you need it.
security.trustedCalloutBody: Only add ranges you fully control. If you run behind a reverse proxy, set <cd>TRUST_PROXY</cd> (or <cd>TRUST_PROXY_HOPS</cd>) first — otherwise every visitor can look like one private IP and bypass two-factor.
security.trustedEmptyBody: When you add a network range here, requests from those IPs will skip rate limits, account lockout, and two-factor.
security.blockedDesc: Blocked addresses are refused everywhere. Automatic blocks expire on their own and are then labeled Expired — remove them whenever you want to tidy the list. Manual blocks stay until you remove them.
security.blockedEmptyBody: Manually blocked addresses will appear here. Automatic blocks also show up while they are active.
security.blockedEmptyNote: No addresses are currently refused manually.
security.kindAuto: Automatic — placed by the failed-sign-in rule
security.neverStays: Never — stays until you unblock it
security.addKeyHint: Add an AbuseIPDB key under Policies to score addresses
security.clearLapsedBody: Automatic blocks that have already run out are removed from the list. Running and permanent blocks are not touched, and an address that misbehaves again is blocked again.
security.permanentBodyExpired: This block has already expired. Making it permanent re-arms it, and it then stays until you unblock this address.
security.permanentBodyActive: This block currently expires {{date}}. It will become a manual block that stays until you unblock this address.
security.makePermanentFailed: Unable to make the block permanent

storage.headDescription: Where thumbnails live, and which folders libraries may be created in.
storage.thumbDesc: Generated covers and previews are written here, separate from original library files.
storage.binDesc: One folder for every library's deleted files, instead of a hidden <cd>.trash</cd> inside each library — which other apps reading the same folders will index and show as though nothing had been deleted.
storage.containersDesc: Containers are approved root folders. Libraries can use the whole container or any folder inside it.
storage.deleteBlockedTitle: Remove all libraries using this container first
storage.saveSettingsFailed: Unable to save Digital Library settings
storage.thumbModalIntro: Choose a writable folder for generated covers and previews. In Docker, use the container path.
storage.containerModalIntro: Choose an existing server folder that libraries are allowed to scan. In Docker, use the container path.

tags.headDescription: Free-form labels scanned from your files, across every library.
tags.intro: Tags are the descriptive layer for your library and can also be created from scanned genres. Rename to fix typos (renaming onto an existing tag merges them) or delete to remove a tag from all books. Renaming a tag that is also a category keyword won't re-sort books — use "Re-match all books" on the Categories tab afterward if needed.
tags.emptyList: No tags yet. Create one here or scan books to import their genres.
tags.modalNote: New tags start unused and can be assigned from a book's metadata editor.
tags.deleteBody_one: This removes the tag from {{count}} book. Books and files are not affected.
tags.deleteBody_other: This removes the tag from {{count}} books. Books and files are not affected.

trashRoot.saveFailed: Unable to save the Recycle Bin location
trashRoot.intro: Browse to a folder inside a Digital Library container, but <bold>not</bold> inside a library — anything in a library is scanned, so deleted files would be catalogued straight back in. Clear it to go back to each library's own hidden <cd>.trash</cd> folder.
trashRoot.infoTitle: Best set before you create libraries
trashRoot.infoBody: The location can only change while the Recycle Bin is completely empty, so once you are using it, moving it means restoring or permanently deleting everything in it first. Nothing already deleted is moved by a change — every item remembers where its own files went.
trashRoot.warnTitle: Keep it on the same storage as your libraries
trashRoot.warnBody: Deleting into a bin on the same disk is an instant rename. To another disk it is a real copy of every byte, so deleting a large video, or a duplicate cleanup removing thousands of photos, will take much longer.
trashRoot.pickerIntro: Choose a folder inside an approved container — one outside every library, since anything inside a library is scanned.

users.restoredNotice: This email belonged to a deleted account, so {{name}} takes it over — anything it still owns, like libraries or collections, comes with it. Its old two-factor setup and passkeys were removed.
users.noMfa: This user doesn't have two-factor on
users.cannotDelete: This user cannot be deleted here
users.roleLockedBody: This administrator role is protected from changes here.
users.deleteBody1: This will deactivate the account and sign the user out on all devices.
users.deleteBody2: Libraries, groups, activity history, and files are not deleted.
users.windowTitle: Allow "{{name}}" to link a device from outside?
users.windowIntro: They can sign a TV, display or kiosk in from anywhere, instead of only from your home network. It ends as soon as one device is linked, or when the time below runs out — whichever comes first.
users.windowRange: Between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes. Long enough to walk someone through it; short enough that forgetting costs nothing.
users.windowNote: <bold>They will still need their own password to authorize it</bold>, and the linked device still can't reach the control panel or authorize others. You'll be emailed if one is linked.
users.mfaBodyEmail: This turns off two-factor and clears their backup codes along with the emailed-code setting.
users.mfaBodyApp: This turns off two-factor and clears their backup codes along with their authenticator.
users.mfaBodyBold: They'll sign in with just their password until they set it up again.
users.pkBody_one: This removes their passkey — for when they've lost the device that held it.
users.pkBody_other: This removes all {{count}} of their passkeys — for when they've lost every device that held one.
users.pkBodyBold: Their password and two-factor sign-in still work, and they can add a new passkey afterwards.

quotes.headDescription: Bring in quote packs for the family to read, and take one back out if it turns out to be full of rubbish.
quotes.empty: No packs imported yet. Import one to fill the quote of the day.
quotes.deleteBody_one: This deletes the {{count}} quote still here from that import, wherever it appears — the Quotes page, the quote of the day, and any collection holding it. Quotes typed in by hand and passages highlighted while reading are not affected, and the file can always be imported again.
quotes.deleteBody_other: This deletes the {{count}} quotes still here from that import, wherever they appear — the Quotes page, the quote of the day, and any collection holding them. Quotes typed in by hand and passages highlighted while reading are not affected, and the file can always be imported again.
